title: Austin's 1909 Infrastructure and Election Plans
summary:
• **Election officials appointed and compensated**: The city council unanimously approved an ordinance establishing judges and clerks for elections over the next two years, setting their pay at $2 per day for an eight-hour shift.

• **Temporary ford planned during bridge work**: With the Colorado River bridge undergoing removal, the mayor was authorized to coordinate with county officials to establish a temporary ford at Shoal Creek's mouth and install arc lights on both sides for public safety.

• **East 4th Street platform approved**: A petition to construct a platform on East 4th Street was granted with overwhelming support (10-1 vote), despite one alderman's attempt to delay the decision.

• **Refund request pending review**: A citizen's request for pound fee refunds was referred to the Claims & Accounts Committee for further investigation.

in platform on East 4th St.
By Alderman Moore Petition of A P Martin & J A Martin asking permission to put in a
platform on East 4th street. Alderman Cuneo moved that the petition lie on the table until
the next regular meeting, which motion was lost by thre following vote :
Yeas Aldermen :Cuneo & Wilhelm 2
Nays Aldermen Armstrong, Crooker, Haynes, Miller, Moore, Petri, Redd, Scott & Smith 9 The

Nays Alderman Cuneo 1
Judges & Clerks of
Election
approved
The Mayor laid before the Council an ordinance appointing Judges and Clerks of election
for the next two years, and fixing their compensation.
The ordinance was read the first time, and on motion the rule was suspended and the
ordinance placed on its second reading by the following vote : Yeas Aldermen Armstrong,
Crooker, Cuneo, Haynes, Miller, Moore, Petri, Redd
Scott, Smith & Wilhelm 11
Nays none. The ordinance was read the second time . Compensation of Judges
of Election
The blanks giving names of Judges and Clerks were then filled .
On motion the compensation of Judges and Clerks was fixed at $ 2,00 per day of eight
hours, or the fractional part of a day.
The ordinance as amended was then passed under suspension of the rule by the following
vote : Yeas Aldermen Armstrong, Crooker, Cuneo , Haynes, Miller, Moore, Petri, Redd,
Scott, Smith & Wilhelm 11
Nays none .
Ford at mouth of
Shoal Creek
Alderman Haynes moved that the Mayor be authorized and requested to confer with the
Commissioners Court of Travis County in regard tom the ford across the Colorado River at
the mouth of Shoal creek, which will have to be used by the public during the time of the
removal of the Colorado bridge, and also that he confer with the Water & Light Commission
as to placing an Arc light on each side of the river at such ford , which motion was
adopted. Arc Lamps, etc.
Ordinance paying expenses
of Dr. Loving & Washington
By Alderman Armstrong an ordinance appropriating the sum of $ 50,00 for the purpose of
paying Dr Loving’s expenses to Washington, which was read and referred to the Finance
Committee.
On motion the Council adjourned.
W. A. Johnson
